source: If moral responsibility requires alternative possibilities, then an agent who could not have done otherwise is not responsible. An objector claims that every responsible action requires alternative possibilities. But consider a case in which a hidden intervener would have forced the agent to act if the agent had hesitated. The agent acted on their own reasons and the intervener never acted. The agent could not have done otherwise. Nevertheless, the agent is morally responsible. Therefore, moral responsibility does not always require alternative possibilities.
